bodyText: AI at School ERASMUS+ Home Teacher handbook Competencies Letter to principals ERASMUS+ PROJECT · POLAND × CZECHIA Learn with AI, think for yourself. A project for lower secondary (ages 11-15) and upper secondary school students (15-19). We educate the whole school community in the proper use of artificial intelligence while developing and protecting students' cognitive and creative skills. Open the teacher handbook Letter to school principals of young people (16-24) in the EU use generative AI 64% of young people (16-24) in the EU use generative AI of young people in Czechia, 59% for formal education 78% of young people in Czechia, 59% for formal education AI Act: AI literacy duty in force since 2 Feb 2025 Art. 4 AI Act: AI literacy duty in force since 2 Feb 2025 TARGET GROUP 11-15 years · 15-19 years WHAT YOU WILL FIND ON THIS SITE Three parts of the project Letter for school principals Why the programme matters, what it brings to students and teachers, an invitation to consultations, and charts built from European data. Read the letter Interactive AI handbook for teachers AI basics, effective prompts, lesson planning, classroom activities, useful tools, ethics, quizzes and exercises. Open the handbook Competencies AI cannot replace What to teach students aged 11-15 and 15-19: critical and creative thinking, own opinions and collaboration, backed by research. See the recommendations EVIDENCE BASE Five findings every staff member should know These five research findings are the backbone of the whole project. Each recommendation in this handbook and in the competencies section builds on them. 1 Neurocognitive impact of LLMs EEG data show weaker brain connectivity and poorer recall of one’s own essay when it is written with an LLM. Students who switched from an LLM to no tools struggled to quote their own text (Kosmyna et al., 2025, MIT). SOURCE: KOSMYNA ET AL., 2025 2 Expert deskilling is measurable In Polish colonoscopy centres, doctors who routinely used AI detected fewer adenomas when working without it, about 28% down to 22% (Budzyń et al., 2025, Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology). Deskilling appears even in experts. SOURCE: BUDZYŃ ET AL., 2025 3 Automation bias in verification Knowledge workers who trust GenAI more apply less critical thinking; those confident in their own skill apply more. Thinking shifts from producing to verifying, which only works if the person still knows enough to verify (Lee et al., CHI 2025). SOURCE: LEE ET AL., CHI 2025 4 Gradual societal disempowerment Researchers describe no dramatic AI takeover, but a slow erosion of human influence as AI replaces human cognition in the economy, culture and the state. The loss of individual thinking skills is the micro-level of that risk (Kulveit et al., 2025). SOURCE: KULVEIT ET AL., 2025 5 A legal mandate: EU AI Act, Art. 4 Since 2 February 2025, providers and deployers of AI systems, including schools, must ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and of people acting on their behalf. Schools are writing their rules right now. SOURCE: REGULATION (EU) 2024/1689, ART. 4 A note on the evidence Most studies are still small, short-term or correlational; long-term causality is not yet established. That is exactly why we recommend practical, testable classroom interventions rather than bans or blind adoption. The full source list is on the competencies page. FIRST PART OF THE PROJECT Letter to school principals Dear principal, allow us to introduce the AI at School project. It is aimed at lower secondary school students (11-15) and upper secondary school students (15-19), and its goal is to educate the whole school community, students and teachers alike, in the proper use of artificial intelligence. At the same time, we want to develop and protect students' cognitive and creative skills at a time when generative AI is becoming their everyday tool. The project is carried out by Polska Rada Organizacji Młodzieżowych and Česká rada dětí a mládeže in cooperation with academic institutions and is funded by European grants (Erasmus+). Why implementing the programme matters Generative AI went from novelty to default tool for young Europeans in under three years. In 2025, 64% of EU citizens aged 16-24 used a generative AI tool in the last three months, almost double the 33% of all adults. In Czechia it was 78%, and 59% used it for formal education (Eurostat, 2025). AI can boost the work efficiency of students and teachers and raise student engagement, but research also shows a cost: heavy AI users offload more thinking and score lower on critical thinking, and the effect is strongest in the 17-25 age group (Gerlich, 2025). That is why AI should be neither simply allowed nor banned, but used consciously, with clear school rules. Invitation to consultations We would be glad to consult the programme and a course on its proper implementation with you and your team. The project is open to changes so that it complies with the needs and rules
